info.name: Kraken
account_import
Use this endpoint to stage account data before creating an account.

items.docs: As the name suggests, this endpoint stores the data in Kraken but does not create an account from the data. Staged account data can be updated as many times as you like before an account is created.

info.name: Use this endpoint to process staged account data into an account in Kraken.

items.docs: The endpoint accepts a JSON payload that contains an object referencing existing staged account data. The `operations_team_name` that the account should be linked to should also be provided. An optional `dry_run` field is available to test the account creation process without actually creating the account. This is useful for testing the process to ensure that an account would be created successfully.

info.name: Use this endpoint to add notes to an account.

items.docs:
Some points to note:
- A note must contain at least one of the fields `body` or `document_paths`.
- A `created_at` datetime may optionally be provided. Otherwise, it will default to the current local time.
- The `document_paths` refer to the locations in S3 where attached documents are stored.
- An optional `is_pinned` boolean can be passed in the payload to control whether this note will be pinned to the top of the Kraken account support site page.

Submit registration flows for meter points

params.name: external_account_number
params.description: The account number in the source system.

params.name: import_supplier_code
params.description: The code of an existing Import Supplier.

items.docs: Use this endpoint to submit registration flows for meter points on an existing imported account. Note that this endpoint marks meter points to be registered. Kraken will then pick up these meter points and attempt to register them. Given a successful response from this API, it is still possible for the registration process to fail downstream.

info.name: Use this endpoint to import financial transactions to an account.

params.name: check_previously_added
params.description: Boolean flag indicating whether to check if a transaction has already been added.

params.name: force_add_to_current_statement
params.description: boolean flag. If set to true and the payload contains a transaction that is outside the currently-open statement period, this will modify the transaction date so that it is within the currently-open statement period. This then allows the transaction to be added to the statement instead of throwing an error. A description is added to the transaction to explain this, and a note is pinned to the account.

items.docs: Use this endpoint to import financial transactions to an account.
